item: Intermittent failures of the hosted `go test 1/2` shard (cmd/kudurru and ee/edge/dnsdist) that keep the PR from a reliably green CI
summary: Gate G04 needs hosted CI green on the final head, and the tracker forbids loosening or skipping tests. The `go test 1/2` job (runner ubicloud-standard-4-ubuntu-2404, 4 vCPUs, race detector, cmd/kudurru split into 7 batches of 94 tests by hack/go-test.py) fails intermittently with a rotating set of tests. Of the last twelve completed ci runs on the branch, eight failed on their first attempt. Evidence collected on 2026-11-11 under $SHARED/evidence/INTEGRATE-1/: (1) hosted-de0d249a-gotest1.log (first batch of this completion pass, attempt 1): TestRunServeQuerylogFailedPrepareKeepsOldCompleteRoute failed with `ops: listen tcp 127.0.0.1:42457: bind: address already in use`, and TestCLIOIDCBrowserActualTLSProofRefusals/nonce failed with `serving_http_oidc_test.go:113: browser writer ended context canceled`. (2) hosted-de0d249a-gotest1-attempt2.log: both passed, and TestServingHTTPClusterActivationIdentityRefusalAndRollback/invalid-member failed with `serving_command_test.go:73: primaryruntime: required adapter/publication unavailable`. (3) hosted-19bfecc4-gotest1-prebatch.log (a docs-only commit one before the base 33ee04bc, so pure baseline): TestServingHTTPAuthCookieFactorAndPasswordClears/confirm failed with `serving_http_auth_reload_test.go:400: HTTP status: got 401, want 204`, and TestSupervisorLifecycle (ee/edge/dnsdist) failed with `supervisor_test.go:208: 4 starts, want 2 for validated named-member staging`. Earlier retained hosted logs show the same classes before this pass: the port collision in .context/hosted-release-73d4b057-20261109/job-128928630045-raw01.log (TestOfflineAnchorRecoveredTrustServesAfterRestart), and `primaryruntime: required adapter/publication unavailable` in .context/hosted-ffd18d41-20261109/42568583609-attempt1-failed.log (TestDoctorNotifyCannotAdoptNewPublicationKeysOrWriter/writer, `primary driver ended early`). The OIDC failure is the exception: it was NOT found in any earlier retained hosted log, and it reproduced locally on the pushed head de0d249a once in 30 runs (`taskset -c 0-3 go test -race -count=30 -run '^TestCLIOIDCBrowserActualTLSProofRefusals$' ./cmd/kudurru`, 899 s, subtest `multi` that time; log oidc-repro-head-de0d249a.log). No valid run on the base exists yet (oidc-repro-base-INVALID-ran-whole-suite.log is a botched control and proves nothing). The batch that was pushed between 33ee04bc and de0d249a changed code on the writer path: cmd/kudurru/serving_anchor_activation.go, serving_anchor_follower*.go, serving_anchor_updater.go, querylog_runtime.go, serving_member_objects.go, serving_update_output.go, serving_runtime.go, internal/store/sqlite member command output, and the query-log sink host.
alreadyDone: A read-only control checkout of the base commit exists at /home/vercel-sandbox/kudurru/.context/wt/base-33ee04bc (detached at 33ee04bc). Never edit it. You may run tests in it through the heavy wrapper to compare the base with the head.

hack/go-test.py prints each batch as `Command batch N/7: name, name, ...`; the exact hosted batches that contained two of the failures are saved as -run regular expressions in $SHARED/evidence/INTEGRATE-1/batch-oidc.txt and batch-querylog.txt, so a hosted batch can be replayed locally in the same process composition.

remaining.title: Find why the serving writer ends with `context canceled` while its own context is alive (TestCLIOIDCBrowserActualTLSProofRefusals), decide whether the first completion batch introduced or worsened it, and fix the cause
remaining.detail: The fixture at cmd/kudurru/serving_http_oidc_test.go:108-116 runs `s.RunWriter(ctx)` under an elector and reports `browser writer ended` when RunWriter returns a non-nil error while the test's ctx is not canceled. RunWriter (cmd/kudurru/serving_lifecycle.go:234-272) only returns an error that is not `transientServing`; writerEpisode runs an errgroup whose first error wins. So some component of the writer episode returned context.Canceled as a first error, or resetWriter/writerCurrent did, without the outer context ending. Step 1, establish the facts before changing anything: measure the failure rate on the head and on the base control checkout with the same command, pinning and count (at least 60 runs each, through the heavy wrapper, one at a time; write a small script file for it so that shell precedence cannot change what runs), and replay the hosted batch (batch-oidc.txt) on both. If the base never fails, bisect the 62 commits between 33ee04bc and de0d249a (`git log --oneline 33ee04bc..de0d249a`) at the package boundaries first (CI/qualification, forwarding fixes, managed anchors, query-log sink fan-out, docs). Step 2, find the mechanism by instrumenting a scratch copy of the test or the runtime (never commit diagnostics): which component returned the canceled error, and whose cancellation it was. Step 3, fix the cause in the product if a component leaks an inner cancellation as a writer failure (that would make a real writer exit and be re-elected for no reason, which is a product defect, not only a test problem), or fix the fixture if the test is wrong; do not widen `transientServing`, add retries or loosen the assertion to hide it. State plainly in your result whether the batch introduced it, worsened it, or it predates the batch, with the numbers.
remaining.acceptance: A test that reproduces the mechanism deterministically (not statistically) and fails before the fix; the original test passes at least 200 consecutive runs under race pinned to 4 CPUs after the fix (log kept); the hosted batch replay passes 5 times; the writer, anchor, member and query-log root selections still pass. If the cause is in code of the first batch, name the commit.

remaining.title: Remove the free-port race from the mounted test harnesses (`bind: address already in use`)
remaining.detail: The mounted tests choose listener addresses with offlineFreeAddress (and similar helpers in test/e2e and internal/testutil/kudurrutest): listen on port 0, read the port, close, then hand the number to runServe or to a child process, which binds it later. Another test or process can take the port in between; cmd/kudurru runs 94 tests per process, and e2e starts several nodes. Failures seen: hosted `ops: listen tcp 127.0.0.1:42457: bind: address already in use` (TestRunServeQuerylogFailedPrepareKeepsOldCompleteRoute), hosted 73d4b057 (TestOfflineAnchorRecoveredTrustServesAfterRestart), and a local e2e run where node conflict-c's metrics port was already in use ($SHARED/evidence/QUAL-CI/e2e08-licensed-prebuilt.log). Fix it at the root for in-process mounts and for child processes: prefer `127.0.0.1:0` with the bound address read back from the running server where the configuration and readiness plumbing allow it (the metrics and internal listeners already do this in mountedTestConfig); where a test must know the address before start, hand over an already bound listener, or allocate from a process-wide and cross-process reservation that cannot hand the same port out twice and keeps the port held until the server binds (for example SO_REUSEPORT hand-over is NOT acceptable in production code paths: keep any such mechanism in test helpers only). Do not add a blind retry of the whole test. Production listener code may gain a small, clearly test-neutral seam (an injected listener) only if it does not change production behavior; say so in your result.
remaining.acceptance: A stress test that starts many mounted fixtures concurrently in one process and many in parallel processes (go test -count with -parallel and several processes at once) shows zero bind collisions over at least 2,000 allocations where the old helper shows collisions under the same stress (keep both logs); every caller of the old helpers in cmd/kudurru, test/e2e, test/interop and internal/testutil is converted or shown not to race; the root selections that use mountedTestConfig pass.

remaining.title: Find and fix the cause of `primaryruntime: required adapter/publication unavailable` ending a primary driver or refusing a command early in mounted tests
remaining.detail: Seen hosted on de0d249a attempt 2 (TestServingHTTPClusterActivationIdentityRefusalAndRollback/invalid-member, serving_command_test.go:73) and before this pass on ffd18d41 (TestDoctorNotifyCannotAdoptNewPublicationKeysOrWriter/writer, primary_runtime_test.go:170, `primary driver ended early`) and b2d197d8. Find where the error is produced (internal/primaryruntime), which startup or publication ordering makes a required adapter or publication absent for a short time on a slow 4-CPU runner, and whether a real node can hit the same window (a primary driver that ends early on a real node would be a product defect: say which it is). Reproduce by constraining CPUs (taskset -c 0-1 or 0-3, GOMAXPROCS) and replaying the hosted batch compositions; then fix the ordering or the fixture. No retries, no loosened assertions.
remaining.acceptance: Deterministic reproduction of the mechanism in a test that fails before the fix; both named tests pass 200 consecutive runs under race pinned to 2 and to 4 CPUs; the primary runtime, doctor, cluster activation and serving command selections pass.

remaining.title: Find and fix the two baseline intermittent failures seen on 19bfecc4: the cookie factor confirm answering 401, and the dnsdist supervisor lifecycle start count
remaining.detail: (a) TestServingHTTPAuthCookieFactorAndPasswordClears/confirm: `serving_http_auth_reload_test.go:400: HTTP status: got 401, want 204`. A TOTP confirm answered 401: look for a time-step boundary (a code generated at the end of one 30-second step and checked in the next, replay floor, or the test clock), a publication the session had not reached yet, or request-budget state shared between subtests. If a real user can hit the same refusal with a valid code, it is a product defect: fix it there. (b) TestSupervisorLifecycle in ee/edge/dnsdist: `supervisor_test.go:208: 4 starts, want 2 for validated named-member staging`, `:221: 4 starts after an unchanged rendered set, want 2`, `:267: want two clean stops`. The supervisor restarted its child more often than the test expects on a slow runner: find whether the supervisor really restarts dnsdist unnecessarily (product defect: an edge that restarts under load drops queries) or the fake child and the test's timing are at fault. Reproduce each with constrained CPUs before changing anything; no retries and no loosened assertions.
remaining.acceptance: For each: the mechanism is reproduced deterministically in a test that fails before the fix, and the original test passes 200 consecutive runs under race pinned to 2 and to 4 CPUs (logs kept). The auth reload/factor selection and the ee/edge packages pass.

recommendation: Root-cause each failure; treat every one as a possible product defect until the mechanism shows otherwise. FLAKE-OIDC-WRITER first, because it is the only one that may come from the batch just pushed and nothing more is pushed until that is known.
sharedSeams: cmd/kudurru/serve_mount_test.go and serve_offline_test.go (many lanes add mounted tests that call mountedTestConfig and offlineFreeAddress: keep the helper names and signatures working)
testInfra: Use the heavy wrapper for every run in ./cmd/kudurru (see AGENT-BRIEF.md section 5). Long repetition runs must be started with run_in_background and a script file, one at a time, never several unbounded runs at once and never the whole package with -count greater than 1: an uncontrolled full-suite repetition on this shared machine disturbs every other lane's timing-sensitive tests. Constrain CPUs with `taskset -c 0-3` (the hosted runner has 4 vCPUs). Replay a hosted batch with: go test -race -count=1 -timeout 30m -run "$(cat $SHARED/evidence/INTEGRATE-1/batch-oidc.txt)" ./cmd/kudurru (about 5 minutes).
risks: Intermittent failures invite statistical 'fixes' (longer deadlines, retries): those are not acceptable here; find the mechanism.
A base control only means something if it runs exactly the same command as the head; script it.
Other lanes are adding mounted tests concurrently; a harness change must keep existing helper call sites compiling.
